issues.passage: Once the brass section covered the theme completely, the motif became especially conspicuous.
issues.why: In musical English, when the brass 'covers' a theme it states/carries that theme, so the motif becoming especially conspicuous is natural correct use of conspicuous = clearly audible/attracting notice. Not a valid distractor.

fix.correctPassage: The senator's bright red scarf made her conspicuous among the gray coats on the steps.
wrongPassages: She kept the signed originals conspicuous in a locked vault no one ever opened.
The courier hid the package so thoroughly that it was conspicuous to every passerby.
His muted, camouflaged jacket was chosen to be as conspicuous as possible in the forest.
